solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bloke, one that's turned up late for work

parts.note: a bloke is a man
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is flipped round to run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow who rolls up late for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' acts on 'up' alone, giving PU; the phrase 'turned up late' looks like arriving late but splits into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something, like clay or a lever, is to handle it skilfully, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Bloke ignoring European murder? That's spite

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for European is left out of the word for bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a male
ice is slang for kill or murder

explanation.surface: A man killing someone abroad, and the question of motive: was it spite?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the E from MALE, leaving MAL; ICE as 'murder' is underworld slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, the wish to hurt someone, a close synonym of spite.

clue.text: Gold in Alaskan city? Not now

indicators.note: in means the heraldic word for gold sits within the Alaskan town's name

parts.note: Nome is a city in Alaska, famed for its gold rush
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Gold in an Alaskan city? Not any longer, the rush is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Nome really was a gold-rush town, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens never again has ceased: it is not now and not afterwards either.

clue.text: Uprising uncommonly identified in pastoral events

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellion that turns up oddly in rustic gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges PASTORAL EVENTS. The Peasants' Revolt was the English rising of 1381 led by Wat Tyler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peasants' Revolt is a famous example of an uprising, the 1381 rebellion against the poll tax.

clue.text: Brainy lot, nothing less, confounded by hard maze

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed up
less means the zero shape for nothing is taken out of the word lot

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A clever group, empty-handed and baffled by a tricky maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' and 'confounded' work in turn: the zero shape drops out before the shuffle, and 'confounded' doubles as the brainy group's bafflement.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is an intricate network of paths, a synonym of maze.

clue.text: Drunk later today, on going out

indicators.note: going out means the little word on departs from the word for this evening

parts.note: this evening is tonight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning to be drunk later today when out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' removes ON from TONIGHT, leaving the letters for the answer; 'going out' reads like a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for intoxicated, a slang synonym for drunk.

clue.text: Try returning potty

indicators.note: returning means the word for potty is read backwards

parts.note: potty and bats both mean crazy

explanation.surface: An attempt at getting a child back onto the potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses BATS, an informal word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt, so it is a synonym of a go or try.

clue.text: Return of crude force not allowed, securing good athletic contest

indicators.note: Return of means the whole string built from the following pieces is read backwards

parts.note: crude means raw, unrefined
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: securing means holding something within, so the letter for good goes inside

parts.note: a ball or shot ruled out is out, not allowed

explanation.surface: A ban on brute force returning, in the context of some sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns round everything after it, giving RAWFOGUT backwards; 'securing' puts the good letter inside. 'not allowed' as OUT is a ruling, as in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug-of-war is a team pulling contest on a rope, a classic athletic event at sports days.

clue.text: Tour guide? Cook's encompassing latest features of complete world route

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the selected letters go inside

parts.note: a cook is a baker; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: latest features means the final letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Thomas Cook's tours supply a guidebook covering a round-the-world route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's' looks like Thomas Cook, the travel firm, but is a baker; EDE goes inside. Baedeker guidebooks were the classic travellers' handbooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baedeker is a travel handbook, so a guide for a tour, with the question mark flagging the book, not a person.

clue.text: Liqueur and tisanes blended to form cocktail

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters are combined in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Mixing liqueur with herbal teas to make a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges LIQUEUR and TISANES; 'blended' also fits the bar-room surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a well-known mixed drink of tequila, orange juice and grenadine.

clue.text: Proposition two males in meadow

indicators.note: in means the two letters for males sit inside the word for meadow

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
M is the abbreviation for male, so two males are MM

explanation.surface: Making a pass at two men in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposition' reads as a verb in the surface but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemma is a subsidiary proposition proved on the way to a theorem in mathematics.

clue.text: Major European country upset about one sporting contest

indicators.note: about means around, so the numeral goes within
upset means the letters for the country are turned round

parts.note: GB is Great Britain, a European country
one is the Roman numeral I
a league is a sporting competition

explanation.surface: A major European nation upset during a sporting competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GB into BG, then 'about' puts I inside to give BIG. 'Major' looks like a rank or adjective in the surface and is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-league means of the top rank or most important, a synonym for major.

clue.text: Pirate caught men beginning to sing shanty?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a shanty is a sea song, an air

explanation.surface: A buccaneer caught the crew starting up a sea shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer of the Barbary coast, so a pirate.

clue.text: End of snout to disturb fungus

indicators.note: End of means the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to ruffle is to disturb or agitate

explanation.surface: A pig's nose rooting about to unearth a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs really are used to snuffle out truffles, so the picture fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is an edible underground fungus prized in cooking.

clue.text: Do well to manage school sport

indicators.note: Do in the sense of treat or deal with roughly signals that these letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to succeed by coping well in a sport at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' rearranges WELL TO MANAGE; it looks like part of the phrase 'do well'. The Eton wall game is a rough sport unique to Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton wall game is a football-like game played only at Eton College, a sport of one school.

clue.text: Part of weapon that's at the front, with tip of red line inscribed

indicators.note: inscribed means written within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: being at the front is being ahead

indicators.note: tip of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: Part of a weapon at the front, marked with a red line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribed' and 'tip of' do the work; 'that's at the front' looks descriptive of the arrowhead's position but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrowhead is the pointed tip of an arrow, so a component of a weapon.

clue.text: Shaking and rocking initially involved in wharf problem

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: a quay is a wharf

indicators.note: Shaking means the word and is jumbled up
initially means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A wharf shaking and rocking, which is quite a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaking' gives NDA, 'initially' adds R, and 'involved in' places NDAR within; 'Shaking and rocking' reads as a pair of verbs but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a state of perplexity, a dilemma or problem with no clear answer.

clue.text: Attendee struggled, having no teeth

indicators.note: struggled means writhed about, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A guest who had a hard time eating, being toothless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled' rearranges ATTENDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate means toothless; it also names a group of mammals such as sloths and anteaters lacking front teeth.

clue.text: Where a thorny stem is handled confidentially

definitions.text: Where a thorny stem is handled
definitions.meaning: literally, a thorny stalk is gripped beneath the bloom of this flower
secretly, in strict confidence, the old sense of sub rosa

explanation.surface: Handling something prickly, but keeping it quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from Latin sub rosa: a rose hung over a meeting once marked its talk as secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in secret, from the rose as an ancient emblem of secrecy.

clue.text: Councillor, namely, that is linked to King

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation meaning namely
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A councillor, that is to say, someone tied to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official or counsellor in old Muslim states, adviser to the ruler.

clue.text: Dog poster used in demonstration

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the poster goes within the other word

parts.note: a show is a demonstration
a poster is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: A dog featured on a placard at a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb here, and 'demonstration' looks like a protest rather than a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, the same as tailing them covertly.

clue.text: Time of day mostly recalled by hour in city

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the trimmed word is read backwards
mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: evening is a time of day

explanation.surface: A time of day mostly remembered by its hour in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims EVENING to EVENIN; 'recalled' reverses it to NINEVE. Nineveh was the ancient Assyrian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineveh was a great ancient city of Assyria, on the Tigris in modern Iraq.

clue.text: Chinese people call for attention in Eastern capital

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
oi is a shout to attract someone's attention

explanation.surface: Chinese people calling for attention in an Asian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oi!' is an informal British shout to catch someone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, a city of the East.

clue.text: Fairly pale girl in grip of desire

indicators.note: in grip of means held inside, so the girl's name goes within

parts.note: a wish is a desire
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gone rather pale, overcome by longing.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -ish means 'somewhat', which is why 'Fairly' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Wan means pale, and the suffix makes it rather or somewhat so.

clue.text: A name applied to weapon without much consideration

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
a lance is a weapon, a knight's long spear

explanation.surface: Labelling a weapon in a hurry, without much thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with only a quick look means doing it without close thought or scrutiny.

clue.text: Epic story I cover, penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author writing an epic while covering the topic in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is the epic poem of the Trojan War, the archetypal epic tale.

clue.text: Frenchman agreed to accept verse

indicators.note: to accept means taking something in, so the letter for verse goes inside

parts.note: yes is the word said when agreeing

explanation.surface: A Frenchman agreed to take on some poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French given name, so it can stand for a man from France.

clue.text: Not very intellectual book found in central part of stalls?

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the letter for book sits within

parts.note: the stalls of a theatre have rows of seats, and a middle row is in their centre

explanation.surface: A lowbrow book picked up from the middle of the theatre seating.
explanation.walkthrough: The stalls are the ground-floor seats of a theatre; the question mark flags MIDDLE ROW as a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlebrow describes culture that is moderately but not very demanding, so only modestly intellectual.
